title: Bob Kalsu: The OU All-American Who Gave His Life in Vietnam
question: Which former OU football player was killed in the Vietnam War?
answer: Bob Kalsu, OU's All-America tackle in 1967, left the Buffalo Bills to serve in the Army and was killed in Vietnam on July 21, 1970.
summary: Bob Kalsu, OU's 1967 All-America tackle, left the Buffalo Bills for Army service and was killed at Firebase Ripcord in Vietnam on July 21, 1970.
body: Bob Kalsu came to Oklahoma out of Del City High School in 1963 and grew into one of the Sooners' best linemen. As a senior in 1967 he was team captain and an All-America tackle on a 10-1 team that beat Tennessee in the Orange Bowl.
The Buffalo Bills drafted him in the eighth round in 1968. He won a starting job at guard and was named the team's rookie of the year, the kind of debut that suggested a long pro career ahead.

Kalsu had completed ROTC, and after the 1968 season he honored that commitment, entering the Army as a second lieutenant. After artillery training at Fort Sill, he went to Vietnam in late 1969 with the 101st Airborne Division and served with an artillery battery supporting infantry at Fire Support Base Ripcord.

On July 21, 1970, Kalsu was killed by enemy mortar fire at Ripcord. He was 25. His son was born two days later. Sports Illustrated later described him as the only American professional athlete to die in combat in Vietnam, and his name is on the Vietnam Veterans Memorial in Washington.

His sacrifice has not been forgotten. The Bills added him to their Wall of Fame in 2000, the Army named a replacement company at Fort Campbell for him in 2002, and the post office in Del City now carries his name. For Sooner fans, Kalsu stands as a reminder that some of the program's most important legacies were written far from Owen Field.
